title: Environment toolchain descriptors point at a stale release binary
expected_semantics: The toolchain address published in invocation descriptors (target/release/mncs) tracks the current language revision, so ambient capture observes current compiler/runtime behavior.
actual_behavior_limitation: target/release/mncs is dated 2026-09-23 while target/debug/mncs is dated 2026-10-01 on an active extraction branch; descriptors (including this repo's) address release, so environment-driven capture runs a 9-day-old toolchain.
why_capability_matters: Stale-toolchain capture misattributes behavior: observations, source maps, and identities may not match the code under debug.
current_workaround: Explicit MNCS paths (usually the debug binary) for direct and test use; release remains the descriptor default for stability.

host_language_code_required.why: No host code involved; this is a build/Descriptor freshness gap.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: A toolchain freshness contract (descriptor toolchain identity vs language revision, with staleness surfaced in readiness) or a release rebuild cadence tied to language merges.
tests_evidence: descriptor toolchain target/release/mncs dated Sep 23 vs debug binary Oct 1
resolution_criteria: Descriptor toolchains carry a revision identity and staleness is visible, or release artifacts track language HEAD within a documented window.
